<subject>Re: Outcome of the Insolvency Hearing for TCO's Corporate Lending Accounts</subject>
<body>
You should have the message below in your inbox regarding the borrowers on the SME Lending portfolio. Contact Treasury once you confirm if you can utilise the borrower's funds without holding a reserve.
</body>
<quoted>
 -----Original Message-----
From: 	Owen, Julia  
Sent:	Tuesday, 29 April 2025 16:09
To:	Hamilton, Derek; Hutchinson, Ross; Johnston, Laura; Marian Hussain, Debra
Cc:	Sophie Jr., Ed; Mann, Gregory; m796@maroragroup.com; s692@soldynlabs.com; Barker, Mathew; Amy, Joshua; Garza, Kathleen; m789@trinorco.com; j244@trinorco.com; Holmes, Sean A.
Subject:	Outcome of the Insolvency Hearing for TCO's Corporate Lending Accounts

Here is a quick update on how Marora Bank, TCO, insolvency hearing went last week regarding the Corporate Lending issues:

TCO agreed to withdraw the section of their motion related to Corporate Lending. The lender confirmed that Corporate Lending has been servicing their loan repayments and have settled their instalments since the insolvency filing date.
The £1.7 million claim that TCO had included in Halcyon's "offset balance" (i.e. the outstanding fees for Corporate Lending agreements until maturity) was removed from TCO's Motion.
The minimum reserve account monthly balance should no longer be enforced by the lender (Note: Initially TCO seemed to use Corporate Lending's reserve to offset SME Lending and Corporate Lending liabilities). 

I advise you to question TCO's operations team if they insist Corporate Lending must maintain a minimum balance in your reserve account. If any issues arise, please inform me and I will engage our external legal advisors again.

Thanks,
Julia Owen
</quoted>
